name: WHO emergencies
summary: WHO's Ebola emergency of international concern, declared in May, remains in force; no new PHEIC found
state: WHO marked six months since the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak centred on DR Congo was declared a public health emergency of international concern, confirming over 11,000 cases (Sahara Reporters, 15 Nov). Africa CDC said on 15 Nov the outbreak is still not under control (Al Jazeera). Searches to 19 Nov found no new PHEIC in the past 30 days and no pandemic emergency, so a PHEIC in effect keeps Watch.
for_you: Check FCDO travel advice and NaTHNaC guidance before travel to DR Congo and neighbouring countries.
rubric_hit: A PHEIC in effect (Ebola, since May) = Watch

sources.title: Sahara Reporters — WHO confirms over 11,000 Ebola cases, 5,400 deaths in DR Congo
Al Jazeera — Africa CDC says Ebola outbreak in DR Congo still not under control

why: A WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) or 'pandemic emergency' is the top official global health alarm.
drivers: Outbreak spread, IHR Emergency Committee decisions.

rubric.alert: A new PHEIC declared in the past 30 days, or a pandemic emergency declared.
rubric.watch: A PHEIC in effect, or an IHR Emergency Committee convened.
rubric.normal: No PHEIC in effect other than long-running polio.
